facts.text: The Triassic Period lasted from about 251.9 million years ago to 201.4 million years ago.
The Triassic was the first period of the Mesozoic Era and came before the Jurassic Period.
During much of the Triassic, Earth's continents were joined together in one huge supercontinent called Pangaea.
The Triassic climate was mostly hot and dry, with large deserts across the middle of Pangaea.
As Pangaea began to split near the end of the Triassic, some places became wetter.
Dinosaurs first appeared during the Triassic Period.
The first dinosaurs were not the biggest animals around; many were small compared with later Jurassic giants.
Early dinosaurs had legs held under their bodies, which helped them stand and move differently from sprawling reptiles.
Most early dinosaurs walked on two legs, though later dinosaur groups included many four-legged animals.
Dinosaurs were only one branch of a larger reptile group called archosaurs.
Eoraptor lived about 231 to 228 million years ago in what is now northwestern Argentina.
Eoraptor was small and lightly built, measuring about 1.2 to 1.3 meters long.
Eoraptor had different tooth shapes, which suggests it may have eaten both plants and small animals.
Herrerasaurus lived in the Late Triassic in what is now northwestern Argentina.
Herrerasaurus could grow up to about 6 meters long and was a meat-eater.
Coelophysis lived about 215 to 201.4 million years ago in what is now the southwestern United States.
Coelophysis was a small, slender meat-eating dinosaur that could grow up to about 3 meters long.
Plateosaurus lived in the Late Triassic in what is now central and northern Europe.
Plateosaurus was an early sauropodomorph dinosaur with a long neck, small head, and plant-crushing teeth.
Eoraptor ran upright on its hind legs, and its hind limbs were much longer than its forelimbs.
Eoraptor had five fingers on each hand, with three long fingers ending in large claws.
Herrerasaurus had strong hind limbs, long feet, and a stiffened tail that helped it balance while moving fast.
Herrerasaurus had sharp serrated teeth for eating meat.
Plateosaurus had leaf-shaped teeth suited for crushing plant material.
Plateosaurus adults could be very different sizes, from about 4.8 to 10 meters long.
Early dinosaurs shared Triassic habitats with many other reptiles and mammal relatives.
In the Triassic, crocodile-line archosaurs called pseudosuchians were very important land animals.
The first pterosaurs, flying reptiles that were not dinosaurs, appeared during the Triassic.
The first mammal-line animals close to true mammals appeared during the Triassic.
In the Ischigualasto Formation, non-dinosaur plant eaters were more common than early dinosaurs.
The Ischigualasto Formation in Argentina preserves some of the earliest clear dinosaur fossils.
The Ischigualasto Formation was a river-dominated floodplain with seasonal rainfall.
Eoraptor is known from an almost complete, well-preserved skeleton and other fragmentary fossils.
At Ghost Ranch in New Mexico, scientists found hundreds of Coelophysis skeletons in one famous quarry.
The Chinle Formation in the western United States contains many Late Triassic fossils, including early dinosaurs and petrified wood.
The Triassic ended with a major extinction event about 201.4 million years ago.
Many land reptile groups disappeared at or near the end of the Triassic, but dinosaurs survived.
After the Triassic-Jurassic extinction, dinosaurs spread into more habitats and became the dominant large land animals of the Jurassic.
Scientists generally connect the end-Triassic extinction with huge volcanic eruptions in the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province.
Birds are living dinosaurs, but birds evolved much later than the Triassic, during the Jurassic.
